# `silk/testing/observation`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

What a test reads of the host while the test runner watches it.

## When to use
The built-in test runner (`silk.testing.runner`) watches each test with this module, so it can
skip a passing test whose code and inputs did not change. The native providers of files,
environment variables, clocks, randomness, sockets and child processes report to it. You do not
call it from normal code.

## Details
A watch is one buffer that the runner owns, named by one word of the process. While no watch is
active, a report reads that word and returns. While one is active, [`note`](#note) appends a read the
runner can repeat later (a file's contents, whether a path exists, a directory's listing, an
environment variable), and [`mark`](#mark) records that the test used something it cannot repeat, such
as the clock. Reports from several threads take turns on a lock.

A buffer starts with a 32-byte header: its data capacity, the bytes used, the marks (each a
`u64`, little-endian) and the lock word. Each note after it is its kind byte, then the root and
the path, each as a 4-byte little-endian length and its bytes. A note that does not fit sets
[`OVERFLOW`](#OVERFLOW) instead.

## Gotchas
- Only reads through the native providers are seen. A test that calls C directly, or reads the
  host some other way, reads unseen.

Import as `TestObservation` with `import silk.testing.observation as TestObservation`.

<a id="start"></a>

## `start`

```silk
pub unsafe fn start(buffer: *mut u8) -> ()
```

Makes `buffer` the active watch, so the reports that follow go to it.

### Details
`buffer` must hold a header (`HEADER` bytes) whose first word is the capacity of the data after
it, whose other words are zero, and it must stay valid until [`stop`](#stop). `start` does not clear it;
the runner does.

### Gotchas
Only the test runner calls it, between tests.

<a id="stop"></a>

## `stop`

```silk
pub fn stop() -> ()
```

Ends the active watch. The reports that follow do nothing.

### Gotchas
Only the test runner calls it, between tests. A report on another thread that already read the
buffer's address can still write to it, so the runner reads the buffer only after the test's
threads have stopped.

<a id="watching"></a>

## `watching`

```silk
pub fn watching() -> bool
```

Whether a watch is active.

<a id="mark"></a>

## `mark`

```silk
pub fn mark(reason: u64) -> ()
```

Records, in the active watch, that the test used what `reason` names, which it cannot repeat.

### Details
`reason` is one of the marks, such as [`CLOCK`](#CLOCK). Without an active watch it does nothing.

<a id="note"></a>

## `note`

```silk
pub fn note(kind: u8, root: &[u8], path: &[u8]) -> ()
```

Records, in the active watch, that the test read `path` of a provider rooted at `root`, as
`kind` says.

### Details
`kind` is one of [`FILE`](#FILE), [`ENTRY`](#ENTRY), [`LISTING`](#LISTING), [`VARIABLE`](#VARIABLE), [`WRITE`](#WRITE) or [`TEMPORARY`](#TEMPORARY). Without an active watch it
does nothing. When the note does not fit, it marks [`OVERFLOW`](#OVERFLOW).
